test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 8 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Due to 25% reduction in the price of wheat per kg, John is able to buy 5 kg more for Rs.600. What is the original price of wheat per kg?
solution:
**Given:**

Reduction percent in the price of wheat = 25%

Expenses on wheat = Rs.600 

**Formula used:**

Expense = Price × Quantity

⇒ Quantity = Expense/Price 

**Calculation:**

Let the original price = Rs.100a per kg 

⇒ The reduced price of wheat = 100a × 75/100 = Rs.75a per kg

600/75a - 600/100a = 5 

⇒ 104/3a - 26/a = 5 

⇒ 8/a - 6/a = 5 

⇒ 2/a = 5 

⇒ a = 2/5

**∴ The original price per kg = 100a = 100 × 2/5 = Rs.40 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**By Ratio Method

25% = 25/100 = 1/4 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/41863d978316bac4b3a3fc643b30d5fd590fadde05c5e6f1858efc4d1bfbaddd.png] 

Original Quantity = 3 × 5 = 15 kg 

Expense = Rs.600 

**∴ Original price of wheat per kg = Rs.600/15 = Rs.40**
